package_info.package_versions: N/A (malware-as-a-service platform with multiple payload versions)
package_info.why_malicious: Dark Utilities is a malware-as-a-service platform that provides threat actors with ready-to-use payloads for remote access, command execution, DDoS attacks, and cryptomining. The platform is explicitly designed to enable unauthorized control, abuse, and monetization of compromised systems, making the entire suite inherently malicious and unsuitable for any legitimate use.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (upon execution of payload on victim system)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Upon execution, the payload registers the infected system with the Dark Utilities C2 service and establishes persistent command-and-control communications.
malicious_snippets.code_language: python (or compiled binary, depending on payload)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code initiates an outbound connection to the Dark Utilities C2 server, transmits system identification data to register the victim, and maintains a persistent communication channel for ongoing remote control.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Establishing unauthorized, persistent remote control channels to known malicious infrastructure is a primary indicator of malware, enabling attackers to manage compromised systems covertly.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not silently register systems with external C2 services or maintain persistent, unauthorized remote access without user knowledge or consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote administration tools (RATs) in enterprise environments, but only with explicit user consent, strong authentication, and proper authorization.
key_indicators: Outbound connection to known Dark Utilities C2 domains
Automated system registration without user interaction
Persistence of network connection for remote control
No user notification or authentication for remote access

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The payload receives and executes arbitrary system commands sent from the Dark Utilities C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_language: python (or compiled binary, depending on payload)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a command from the C2 server, the code executes arbitrary system commands on the victim machine and transmits the command output back to the attacker's C2 infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Arbitrary remote command execution from an unauthenticated source is a core capability of remote access trojans and is highly indicative of malicious intent, enabling full attacker control.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal applications do not accept and execute arbitrary commands from remote, unauthenticated sources, nor do they transmit command output externally without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools with strong authentication, user awareness, and audit logging.
key_indicators: Remote command execution capability triggered by C2
No user interaction or consent required
Command output exfiltrated to C2 infrastructure
Execution context matches attacker instructions

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The payload launches DDoS attack modules (Layer 4/Layer 7) using methods such as TCP, ICMP, GET, HEAD, and POST floods against specified targets.
malicious_snippets.code_language: python (or compiled binary, depending on payload)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, upon receiving a DDoS command from the C2 server, the code generates high-volume network traffic (TCP, ICMP, HTTP GET/HEAD/POST) targeting specified IPs or domains, resulting in distributed denial-of-service attacks.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Launching DDoS attacks from compromised systems is a criminal activity, directly abusing victim resources to disrupt third-party services and networks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not use the host system to attack external targets or participate in coordinated DDoS campaigns.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Network stress testing tools, but only in controlled, authorized environments with explicit permission.
key_indicators: Automated generation of high-volume network floods
Remote triggering of attack modules via C2
Use of multiple DDoS methods (TCP, ICMP, HTTP)
Target specification received from attacker

execution_context.trigger: runtime (on attacker command via C2 or automatically on startup)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The payload downloads and runs a Monero cryptominer, connecting to pool.hashvault.pro and mining to an attacker-supplied wallet address.
malicious_snippets.code_language: python (or compiled binary, depending on payload)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code downloads a cryptomining binary from a remote source, executes it on the victim system, connects to a Monero mining pool (e.g., pool.hashvault.pro), and uses the victim's CPU/GPU resources to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker's wallet.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthorized cryptomining is a form of resource theft, covertly monetizing compromised systems for attacker profit and degrading system performance.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not mine cryptocurrency or download and execute mining software without explicit user consent and transparency.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cryptomining software installed and run by the system owner with full knowledge and consent.
key_indicators: Silent download and execution of mining software
Connection to known Monero mining pools (e.g., pool.hashvault.pro)
Use of attacker-controlled wallet addresses
Resource-intensive processes initiated without user action

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: The payload includes a Discord token grabber module that collects Discord authentication tokens from the victim system and exfiltrates them to the attacker.
malicious_snippets.code_language: python (or compiled binary, depending on payload)
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code searches local files and environment variables for Discord authentication tokens, collects any found tokens, and transmits them to the attacker's C2 infrastructure for credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Harvesting and exfiltrating authentication tokens is a clear sign of credential theft, enabling attackers to hijack user accounts and bypass security controls.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not access or transmit user authentication tokens without explicit user consent and a valid business purpose.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security auditing tools in controlled environments, with user authorization and data protection measures.
key_indicators: Access to Discord token storage locations and environment variables
Exfiltration of sensitive credentials to C2 infrastructure
Integration of token harvesting with remote attacker control
No user notification or consent for credential access

attack_chain.action: Victim executes the Dark Utilities payload, which registers the system with the C2 service.
attack_chain.leads_to: Establishes persistent remote access and awaits further attacker commands.

attack_chain.action: Attacker issues commands via the C2 panel to execute arbitrary system commands, launch DDoS attacks, start cryptomining, or steal Discord tokens.
attack_chain.leads_to: System is abused for remote control, DDoS, cryptomining, and credential theft.

attack_chain.action: Payload maintains persistence and continues to receive and execute attacker instructions, potentially updating itself or spreading to other systems.
attack_chain.leads_to: Ongoing compromise and monetization of the victim system.

behavioral_signatures: Outbound connections to known Dark Utilities C2 domains (e.g., dark-utilities[.]xyz, dark-utilities[.]pw, dark-utilities[.]me)
Automated registration of new hosts with remote C2 infrastructure without user interaction
Execution of arbitrary system commands received from remote C2 servers
Initiation of DDoS attack traffic (TCP, ICMP, HTTP GET/HEAD/POST floods) to external targets
Silent download and execution of cryptomining software (e.g., xmrig) on victim systems
Access and exfiltration of Discord authentication tokens from local storage or environment variables
file_indicators: Presence of unknown binaries/scripts matching Dark Utilities payload hashes
Files or processes named after common cryptomining software (e.g., xmrig, miner.exe)
Unusual scripts or binaries placed in system startup locations (e.g., Windows Startup folder, Linux init scripts)
Temporary files or dropped executables associated with cryptomining or token grabbing modules
network_indicators: Connections to dark-utilities[.]xyz, dark-utilities[.]pw, dark-utilities[.]me (C2 domains)
Connections to pool.hashvault.pro (Monero mining pool) or other mining pool endpoints
Outbound traffic to Discord API endpoints for token exfiltration (e.g., discord.com/api/v9/auth/login)
Connections to onion or IPFS-based C2 infrastructure as referenced in payload configuration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for outbound connections to known Dark Utilities C2 domains and Monero mining pools. Detect execution of unknown binaries or scripts that match known payload hashes or are placed in startup locations. Look for processes that initiate DDoS attack traffic or download and run cryptomining software. Monitor for access to Discord token storage locations and suspicious exfiltration of credentials to external endpoints. Correlate behavioral indicators such as remote command execution, persistence mechanisms, and resource-intensive processes with file and network indicators to identify active infections.
